Darric rose off his knee. Wrong — flank security held unless called — but Darric had two nephews on a marking crew somewhere in this same wood.
Gray. That was the first of her — skin the gray of weathered heartwood.
She came out of the trunk the way a swimmer comes up through the skin of a pond.
Gray light, no sun to it, the kind that flattened distance and made the glass earn its keep.
He gave up a full second to disbelief, a second he spent standing flat-footed.
Posco had the glass on him now and the man's face held nothing, the mild pleasant blankness of a fellow doing an errand he didn't mind.
His breathing had stopped in the trained way, the pause at the bottom of the exhale where the shot lived.
That was the worst of it, worse than the blood.
